system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Go in production
G2: Python services (Django/FastAPI)
G3: gRPC
G4: Terraform authoring
G5: team lead title

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Claiming production Go or Python service experience to match a Python/Go ad
T2: Listing FastAPI/Django/gRPC because the ad asks for them
T3: Turning the Go side project into professional experience
T4: Calling him team lead because he runs a guild
T5: Claiming Terraform authoring
T6: The old cover letter is addressed to his current employer: writer must not reuse its 'Insurance is new to me' framing

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Software Engineer
Lisbon, Portugal | Email: daniel.okafor-reyes@example.com | Phone: +351 555 010 202 | LinkedIn:
linkedin.com/in/daniel-okafor-reyes-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 7 years of experience designing, building, and operating Java backend services
for insurance and travel products. Experienced with REST APIs, relational databases, Kafka
event-driven integration, automated testing, and cloud deployments on AWS and Kubernetes.
Reduced quote API p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds and introduced safeguards that
eliminated duplicate claim records.
EXPERIENCE
Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech, Lisbon | Jan 2022–Present
• Develop and maintain 7 Java 17 / Spring Boot microservices for policy quoting and claims intake.
• Designed and versioned the REST API for a partner quoting integration used by 12 broker
partners, using OpenAPI.
• Produce and consume Kafka events for the claims workflow; introduced idempotent consumers and
an outbox table, eliminating duplicate claim records.
• Reduced quote endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds by adding Redis caching
and resolving JPA N+1 queries.
• Deploy services to Kubernetes (EKS) with Helm charts through Jenkins pipelines; participate in
an on-call rota one week per month.
Software Developer | Viajar Online S.A., Porto | Sep 2019–Dec 2021
• Built booking and payment features in a Java 11 / Spring MVC monolith backed by Oracle.
• Wrote integration tests with Testcontainers, raising payments-module test coverage from 35% to
70%.
• Helped split the monolith by extracting a notifications service using Spring Boot and RabbitMQ.
Junior Developer (internship then full-time) | CodeFarol Lda, Porto | Jul 2018–Aug 2019
• Maintained PHP and later Java applications for small business clients.
EDUCATION
BSc Informatics Engineering | Atlantic Polytechnic Institute | 2018
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Java (8–17), Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, Kotlin (basic), REST APIs,
OpenAPI, Kafka, RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, Oracle, Redis, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Jenkins, AWS
(EKS, S3, SQS), JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Git, Linux
LANGUAGES
English (fluent), Portuguese (fluent), Spanish (conversational)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am applying for the Backend Engineer role on Tessel Cargo Software’s Routing & Tracking
team. I bring seven years of professional backend experience building and operating Java
services, with practical experience in REST APIs, relational databases, Kafka, automated
testing, and AWS/Kubernetes deployments.
In my current role at Tejo Insurance Tech, I develop and maintain seven Spring Boot
microservices and designed a versioned REST API for a partner integration used by 12 broker
partners. I also work with Kafka events in the claims workflow, where introducing idempotent
consumers and an outbox table eliminated duplicate claim records. By adding Redis caching
and resolving JPA N+1 queries, I reduced quote endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450
milliseconds. These experiences are directly relevant to building reliable event-driven services
and improving the performance of a customer-facing tracking API.
I have also built integration tests with Testcontainers, improved payments-module test
coverage from 35% to 70%, and deployed services to EKS through Helm and Jenkins pipelines.
I am interested in applying this production experience to Tessel’s shipment tracking platform
and its work with carrier events and Kafka event streams. My professional backend experience
is in Java, a comparable language identified in the role requirements, and I am prepared to
contribute that experience to a team whose services are built mainly in Python.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how
my experience with backend services, event-driven integration, performance, and production
operations could contribute to the Routing & Tracking team.
Sincerely,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
